title: Too much context and missing attachments

sections.skill: Notice overloaded requests and missing attachments

questions.prompt: What is context overload?

choices.text: A password that is too long
A tool that is too slow
A request that is short and focused on exactly one clear question
So much loosely related material that the key part gets lost

questions.correct_answer: So much loosely related material that the key part gets lost
questions.intro: Two practical problems spoil many requests. CONTEXT OVERLOAD: pasting huge amounts of loosely related material, so the important part gets lost, or exceeding the context window so some of it is dropped. MISSING ATTACHMENTS: you mention a file ("see the attached schedule") but it never uploaded, uploaded in an unsupported format, or was too large, and the tool answers anyway, sometimes inventing what the file "says." Fixes: include only relevant material, point to the part that matters, and confirm the tool can see the file, for example by asking it to state the file's title or first heading.

sections.skill: Compare overload with packing a suitcase

questions.prompt: Why is an overstuffed suitcase a problem?

choices.text: The thing you need is hard to find
It is the wrong color
Because every single item in it will always be damaged by the extra weight inside
It is too light

questions.correct_answer: The thing you need is hard to find
questions.intro: If you stuff a suitcase with everything you own, the one thing you actually need, your passport, is hard to find and may not even fit. And if you say "my passport is in the suitcase" but forgot to pack it, saying so does not put it there. Requests work the same way: too much material buries what matters, and mentioning an attachment does not mean it arrived.

questions.prompt: Saying "my passport is packed" when it is not is like what?

choices.text: Going on vacation
Packing the passport carefully in an easy-to-reach front pocket of the bag
Mentioning an attachment that never uploaded
Buying a new suitcase

questions.correct_answer: Mentioning an attachment that never uploaded

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Recover from overloaded conversations and failed uploads

questions.prompt: A long conversation covers five topics, and the tool now mixes up instructions. What often works better?

choices.text: Switch topics again
Keep going in the same conversation and add another ten messages of new instructions
Start fresh with a short summary of what matters
Repeat every old message

questions.correct_answer: Start fresh with a short summary of what matters
questions.intro: Overload can also come from long conversations: dozens of messages about different topics, so earlier instructions compete with newer ones. Starting a fresh conversation with a short summary of what matters often works better than continuing an overloaded one. For attachments, watch for answers that are vague where the file would give specifics, which can mean the file was not read. If a product shows an upload error or a "file too large" message, the answer that follows may be based on nothing at all.

questions.prompt: After a "file too large" error, the tool gives a detailed answer about the file. What is the risk?

choices.text: The file was read twice
No risk, because detailed answers always prove the file was read in full
The answer is official
The answer may be based on nothing

questions.correct_answer: The answer may be based on nothing
